Subject: Discovery recap - FinBot inference cost pressure & next steps

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and the next steps we discussed so we all stay aligned. Please flag anything I missed.

Summary of pain points
- Unit economics: current per-token cost is a pain point — you mentioned ~200M tokens/month and the bill has become a hard constraint on product growth.
- Latency & CX: 95th percentile latency spikes affecting conversational flows (target is <300ms ideally).
- Operational friction: current stack makes it hard to test quantized variants quickly and routing between cheaper/expensive variants.

Current stack (as you described)
- Serving: SageMaker-hosted endpoints running a ~13B model for production.
- Tooling: some in-house caching, homegrown autoscaling; limited observability into per-route token cost.

Success criteria for a pilot
- 2–3x reduction in per-token unit cost or clear path to that through batching, KV/prefix caching, and quantization while keeping qualitative quality within your thresholds.
- Maintain 95p latency <300ms for the primary customer flow.
- Reproducible eval set + acceptance criteria agreed up front.

Quantization & batching openness
- You said you're open to 8-bit/4-bit quantized variants as long as we validate quality on a representative prompt set. Also interested in prefix caching for common prompts.

Next steps (agreed)
1) Alex — send a representative prompt/workload sample and a short list of top 10 production prompts (you mentioned you'll share the sample CSV).
2) Redwood (Ben + Dev) — review the prompt sample and send a 2-week POC proposal (scope, targets, and a preliminary cost estimate).
3) Sync: technical deep-dive to scope batching/caching approach and confirm telemetry we need to collect.

Proposed timeline: kickoff next week (week of 2/23) with a 2–3 week POC to demonstrate unit-cost delta.

I'll track the items below and follow up with a short POC scope.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Thanks Marissa — this is perfect and captures the call. A few clarifications and answers below.

Clarifications / details
- Monthly volume: ~200M tokens (production), expected growth 20–30% next quarter.
- Peak: ~120 QPS on our chat flow during morning hours.
- Current spend: roughly $1,200 / M tokens (includes infra + inference licensing). We're looking to materially lower that.
- Latency target: <300ms 95p for the chat flow, anything higher degrades conversions.
- Security: data residency is ok for this POC, but we'll need an SOC 2 attestation later if things go well.

Quantization: we are open to 8-bit / 4-bit trials. Quality baseline is important — we'll provide a small labeled evaluation set with accept/reject examples.

I've attached the prompt/workload sample (finbot-prompt-workload-sample.csv) and a short note on which prompts map to the primary user journey.

Proposed immediate next steps
- Please send a short POC scope + success metrics.
- Schedule the tech deep-dive (Priya will join from our infra team).
- If pricing looks reasonable, we'll fast-track procurement for a small POC commitment.

Thanks — looking forward to next steps.

Regards,
Alex Johnson

Hi Alex — thanks for the prompt sample and the clarity on volumes. Attached is a preliminary cost estimate and a proposed POC scope (redwood-inference-cost-estimate-20260220.pdf). High level:

- Goal: demonstrate a 2x–3x effective unit-cost reduction for the chat flow via a combination of continuous batching, prefix caching for the top prompts, and a quantized 8-bit model variant validated against your eval set.
- POC scope (2–3 weeks):
  1) Baseline run on a mirrored traffic sample to measure current unit cost and latency.
  2) Implement batching + KV caching for top N prompts and run quality checks.
  3) Run an 8-bit quantized variant with A/B on a subset of traffic and report quality delta.
  4) Deliver a short TCO comparison and recommendations for production rollout.

Proposed next steps:
- Tech deep-dive: Tue 2/24 10:00 AM PT (we created a calendar invite)
- Provide labeled eval set (Alex) and any additional telemetry you want us to collect in the baseline run.
- We can start POC within 48–72 hours after kickoff.

I've included the estimate and a sample SOW in the attachment. If this looks reasonable, we can route a short MSA + SOW through procurement.
